CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

CALL TO ORDER  Maria Davila, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:45 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Director of Parks and Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria Davila, Vice Mayor Joshua Barron, Council Member Gil
  Hurtado and Council Member Al Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz,
  City Manager Rob Houston, City Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

EXCUSED/ABSENT  Council Member Maria del Pilar Avalos

1
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING  The City Council approved items A & B by motion of Council Member
  Rios and seconded by Council Member Hurtado:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-28-CC entitled A Resolution of the City Council
  of the City of South Gate, approving the Fiscal Year 2024-2025
  Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (“CAPER”);
  and

  b. Authorized the City Manager, or designee, to submit to the U.S.
  Department of Housing and Urban Development the Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025 CAPER.

  Carol Averell, Housing Manager, gave a presentation.

  Council Member Hurtado is disappointed with the continue graffiti and the
  amount of money the city spends for graffiti abatement.

  Council Member Rios questioned if the city would continue applying for
  federal funding.

  Ms. Averell stated that there was an 11% cut for this year for CDBG. The
  city is waiting for the contracts for this fiscal year.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

1
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING CONT’D  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item. Seeing no one step forward; Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos,
  excused.

2
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN  The City Council approved items A & B by motion of Council Member
  Hurtado and seconded by Council Member Rios:

  a. Waived the reading in full and introduced Ordinance No. 2025-01-CC
  entitled An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California amending Title 11, Chapter 11.43 (Accessory Dwelling
  Units and Accessory Structures) of the South Gate Municipal Code;
  and

  b. Accepted the determination that the proposed amendment is Exempt
  from the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) as a
  “ministerial” project pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15268(a).

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, stated Joshua
  Valdez, Associate Planner, will be giving the presentation. This item is
  before City Council because the city has not updated the ADU ordinance
  Accessory Dwelling Units since 2021. There are new laws ever year that
  are passed by the state that amend rules for ADUs across the state and the
  city must comply with the requirements.

  Joshua Valdez, Associate Planner, gave the presentation.

  Vice Mayor Barron thanked Mr. Valdez for the presentation. He stated this
  community is overrun with difficulties with finding parking and the State
  of California is saying there is a housing crisis. He understands the need
  for housing but does not agree to adding more housing.

  Mayor Davia stated the City of South Gate is required to build 8,282 units
  and the city will keep having parking issues.

  Council Member Rios stated that on the governor’s desk is a bill that
  would allow building six-story buildings/housing in neighborhoods which
  would create problems.

  Page 2 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

2
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN CONT’D  Council Member Hurtado stated the City of Jurupa has the same
  population as the City of South Gate and does not understand why the City
  of Jurupa is only required to build 2,400 units and South Gate is required
  to build 8,282 units.

  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item. Seeing no one step forward; Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos,
  excused.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA Steve Soto thanked Council Member Rios for inviting him tonight. Mr.
  Soto has been writing poems and an author for over 60 years. He has been
  a guest poet columnist for the Desert Sun newspaper. A newspaper that
  serves Palm Springs and the Coachella Valley. Mr. Soto wrote and read a
  poem called “Home of the Brave” in response to unconscionable treatment
  of immigrants.

  South Gate resident informed City Council that he was on his bicycle
  heading eastbound on Santa Ana Street between California and Otis where
  he fell forward due to uneven streets. He is requesting the streets to be
  fixed.

  Carlos Gonzalez, Jr., South Gate resident, is a parent and volunteer and is
  speaking on behalf of the American Youth Soccer Organization, also
  known as AYSO. He informed Council that AYSO practice at Hollydale
  Park and is requesting better lighting.

  Heidi Portillo and her son are present tonight reading a statement prepared
  by all the families in NYSO asking for better lighting at Hollydale Park.

  Sergio Sanchez stated his son play for NYSO. The previous parents
  already spoke on the lighting issues at Hollydale Park, but there are other
  issues, for example the men’s restrooms.

  Mario Sanchez and his children are present tonight. Mr. Sanchez stated his
  children are members of AYSO and having children play sports keeps
  them busy and out of trouble. He reiterated about having better lighting at
  Hollydale Park.

  Consuelo Godoy, South Gate resident, is requesting City Council to place
  a flagpole and a flag in front of city hall in memory of Nicolas “Nick”

  Page 3 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
CONT’D  Godoy. Mr. Godoy was a member of the VFW for 20 years. She stated if
  funds are needed to please inform her.

  Juan Contreras also spoke on the conditions of the restrooms at Hollydale
  Park and poor lighting.

EMAILS  Mario Dominguez, South Gate resident, is requesting the City of South
  Gate develop a bike trail on Southern Avenue like the City of Bellflower.
  He stated South Gate is not bike friendly and the Gate buses lack bike
  racks.

  Claudia Rivera, South Gate resident, is questioning Councilwoman
  Avalo’s character for proposing Robert Montalvo to the Parks
  Commission. Ms. Rivera and her family will no longer support Council
  Members Avalos and Rios.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Mayor Davila asked Mr. Costley about Hollydale Park restrooms.

  Mr. Costley will check on Hollydale Regional Park. He mentioned the
  park is farther away from the community and next to the riverbeds. Every
  time the Parks Department places partition doors, they get stolen. The city
  has put thousands of thousands of dollars into doors. Mr. Costley will
  speak with the restroom industry businesses about new and improved
  doors.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, addressed the condition of the
  sidewalk on Santa Ana.

  Mayor Davila requested the street be looked at.

  Council Member Hurtado explained the process on the non-agenda items.

  Mr. Houston explained the chain of command and asked Mr. Costley if he
  was familiar with the folks that spoke tonight.

  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation, stated yes, the parks
  department has liaison information to the AYSO.

  Mr. Costley thanked everyone that was able to attend the new teen room at
  the girls clubhouse. On October 4th there is the Art Walk in front of the
  auditorium. Everyone is invited to attend the opening of the renovated
  Circle Park at 4 p.m. on October 13th. He also mentioned Fireworks show
  at the Halloween event.

  Page 4 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, no updates.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services, no updates.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources, no updates.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police, announced the Third South Gate Annual
  Classic Car Show scheduled for this Saturday at 10 o’clock. He also
  mentioned taking possession of their second Harley-Davidson motorcycle
  courtesy of Office of Traffic Safety.

  Rob Houston, City Manager, informed the public that their comments are
  heard. The AYSO may have a dialogue with the Director of Parks &
  Recreation. He also mentioned the city’s limitations at Hollydale Park due
  to Edison Easement with powerlines.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, nothing to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, mentioned the City Clerk’s Office processes
  passport applications by appointment. Currently the appointments are
  from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and starting this Monday, we will have afternoon
  appointments from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

  Council Member Rios is suggesting AYSO using the LAUSD field or
  exploring other city facilities that have lighting.

  Council Member Rios enjoyed Mr. Soto’s poem. He attended a water
  workshop and stated two thirds of our water comes from Northern
  California. He asked Mr. Costley to speak about the Senior Adult
  Transportation Popup.

  Mr. Costley stated this Friday the city will be connecting the seniors with
  the Metro, local bus and dial-a-ride.

  Council Member Hurtado mentioned the homeless by the riverbed have
  been lighting very loud fireworks. He informed Connie Godoy that Nick
  Godoy was very nice to him. Nick Godoy was a good person. He
  commended the parents for volunteering and having their children in the
  AYSO. He stated speaking to a representative or consultant for the bus
  route regarding bike racks. The consultant stated because the way the bus
  is set up, a permanent rack cannot be placed but will see if a temporary
  rack can be placed.

  Page 5 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Vice Mayor Barron thanked AYSO for attending tonight’s meeting and the
  parents for volunteering.

  Vice Mayor Barron is the President of the SELA Kiwanis and mentioned
  September 30th will be the Second Annual College Fair and Career Fair at
  the Henry C. Gonzalez Auditorium from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. There will
  be over 27 universities, colleges, and workforce development
  organizations. He thanked Supervisor Janice Hanh and Assembly Member
  Solache for their contribution to the event for the scholarships.

  Vice Mayor Barron mentioned that on October 4th Kiwanis is hosting a car
  show as a fundraiser in the City of Bell Gardens, Ford Park. He had the
  opportunity to visit the Western Carpenters Union Center in Carson. He
  attended an event this weekend for the Save America Movement. Food
  distribution is still being done through the SELA Kiwanis Organization
  and Southeast Leadership Foundation.

  Mayor Davila attended the new teen room and thanked Mr. Costley and
  staff for their hard work putting the room together. She is planning to
  attend the Transportation Popup on Friday and thanked the AYSO parents
  for bringing their concerns to City Council.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were approved by motion of
  Mayor Davila and seconded by Council Member Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios, yes
  (voted no on 5); Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council
  Member Avalos, excused.

3
SURPLUS PERSONAL
PROPERTY MGMT  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-29-CC entitled A Resolution of the City Council
  of the City of South Gate declaring the items listed in Attachment B
  (Bicycles & Miscellaneous Items) and Attachment C (Vehicles &
  Equipment) as surplus, obsolete, or unserviceable City personal
  property.

  b. Authorized the City Manager or designee to dispose of the declared
  items through public auction conducted by U.S. Auctions of Ontario,
  CA; and to execute all related documents consistent with budgeted
  appropriations.

  Page 6 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

3
SURPLUS PERSONAL
PROPERTY MGMT CONT’D
  c. Authorized the City Manager or designee to dispose of any items not
  accepted by the auctioneer or failing to sell by using one or more of
  the following methods, as appropriate: recycling/salvage, scrap, inter-
  agency transfer, trade-in/credit, donation to another public agency, or
  landfill, in compliance with applicable laws and City policies.

4
LAW ENFORCEMENT  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-30-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, approving the Los Angeles
  Interagency Metropolitan Police Apprehension Crim Task Force Joint
  Powers Agreement (LA Impact JPA);

  b. The Los Angeles Interagency Metropolitan Police Apprehension
  Crime Task Force Joint Powers Agreement (Contract No. 2025-59-
  CC), thus authorizing the City's Membership in the LA Impact
  Authority; and

  c. Authorized the City Manager to Execute the JPA Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

5
PERSONNEL - MOU BETW
CITY & EMPLEE GROUPS  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-31-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, approving the SGMEA MOU
  (Contract No. 2025-60-CC), SGPMMA MOU (Contract No. 2025-61-
  CC), SGDMA MOU (Contract No. 2025-62-CC), SGPMA MOU
  (Contract No. 2025-63-CC), SGPOA MOU (Contract No. 2025-64-
  CC), and the Executive Terms (Contract No. 2025-65-CC) for the term
  of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the comprehensive successor
  Memorandums of Understanding in a form acceptable to the City
  Attorney.

6
PERSONNEL ADMIN  The City Council approved Resolution No. 2025-32-CC entitled
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California,
  approving and adopting an updated consolidated pay schedule for all full-
  time and selected part-time employees within the CalPERS guidelines
  during Consent Calendar.

  Page 7 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

7
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council approved Resolution No. 2025-33-CC entitled
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California
  during Consent Calendar:

  a. The creation of the full-time Principal Accountant position in the
  Administrative Services Department;

  b. The reclassification of the full-time City Traffic Engineer to the full-
  time Transportation and Capital Improvement Program Division
  Manager in the Public Works Department;

  c. The reclassification of one (1) full-time Principal Civil Engineer
  positions to the full-time Water Resources and Development Division
  Manager in the Public Works Department;

  d. The elimination of the full-time Deputy City Engineer position in the
  Public Works Department; and

  e. Directed staff to update the Consolidated Salary Schedule by adding
  the Principal Accountant, Transportation and Capital Improvement
  Program Division Manager, and Water Resources and Development
  Division Manager Titles, Pay Grades, and Pay Ranges.

8
FINANCIAL MGMT  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a. A Professional Services Agreement (Contract No. 2025-66-CC) with
  Simpler Systems, Inc., to provide financial reporting software
  (“Simpler Platform”) and related professional services with a not-to-
  exceed amount of $51,380 (License $17,500 + Professional Services
  $30,800 + 10% contingency $3,080), and ongoing Monthly License &
  Maintenance of $1,750 (annualized $21,000), subject to annual
  appropriation;

  b. Authorized the issuance of a Purchase Order to Simpler, by a sole-
  source determination based on proprietary functionality and its
  “datapps” architecture and market uniqueness for Eden-based financial
  reporting, pursuant to SGMC § 1.54.510; and

  c. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement, in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

  Page 8 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

9
LAW ENFORCEMENT  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2025-67-CC) with All City Management
  Services, Inc. (“ACMS”), for crossing guard services for a one (1) year
  term, effective July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

10
TRANSPORTATION
PLANNING/ADMIN  The City Council approved a Memorandums of Understanding (“MOU”)
  (Contract No. 2025-68-CC) with Gateway Cities Council of Governments
  (“GCCOG”) for technical assistance for a Regional Early Action Planning
  (“REAP”) Subregional Partnership (“SRP”) 2.0 Program Grant funded by
  Southern California Association of Governments (“SCAG”) during
  Consent Calendar.

11
MINUTES  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. The Special and Regular Meeting minutes of August 12, 2025; and

  b. The Special and Regular Meeting minutes of August 26, 2025.

12
CITY COUNCIL
APPOINTMENTS  The City Council ratified the appointment by Council Member Gil
  Hurtado of Evelyn Martinez to the Citizen Advisory Committee and
  seconded by Mayor Davila.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos,
  excused.
